name: OAuth PKCE absent or downgraded
description:
The authorization server issued an authorization code for a request with no code_challenge at all, or with code_challenge_method=plain. Without S256 PKCE, an intercepted code redeems without the verifier - the interception attack PKCE exists to close. The finding was proven from the captured exchange: response_type=code without an S256 challenge was answered 302 with a code.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's catalogue has no OAuth row; PortSwigger documents OAuth attacks as an Academy topic tested by hand.
remediation: Require PKCE with code_challenge_method=S256 on every authorization code request, and reject plain or absent challenges. Redeem codes only against the matching verifier.

references.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy: OAuth authentication
PKCE: Proof Key for Code Exchange (RFC 7636)
